title: Northstar refocus: 72hr ops briefing and all-staff prep (v0.1)
content:
Purpose
- Rapid re-alignment ahead of mid-quarter checkpoint. 72 hour play to reconcile top-level OKR deltas, surface risky rollouts, and prep a short all-staff session for Tuesday.

High-level ask to leaders
- Come with a single slide or a 5-line note: 1) critical northstar metric we own, 2) single biggest risk this quarter, 3) 1 ask from execs to unblock us. Keep it tight.

Why now
- Observed drift in signal between product usage trends and expected throughput improvements from Dedicated rollout. Cost plan vs telemetry mismatch. Need to avoid widening gap into next quarter.

72hr cadence overview (timeline)
Day 0 (Friday afternoon) - Ops triage + anchor doc
- Publish this brief and a short Loom summarizing the 3 asks.
- Slack channel: #northstar-72hr-refocus (pinned messages: schedule, templates).
- Quick intake: accept up to 3 slides per functional leader by EOD Monday.

Day 1 (Saturday) - Asynchronous work window
- Leaders draft short notes in drive doc; product and infra add telemetry snippets. No meetings unless critical.

Day 2 (Sunday) - Review window by small exec panel
- Exec panel: CTO, Head of Product, CRO, COO review slides and tag items for deep dive. Use comments in Drive.

Day 3 (Monday) - Finalize material + rehearsal
- Merge comments, finalize the all-staff 15 minute slot and an optional 30 min follow-up breakout.
- Rehearsal 11:00-11:30 PT for presenters.

Day 4 (Tuesday) - All-staff 15 minute sync + breakout
- Format: 8 minute concise update from founders/execs, 5 minute callouts from 3 function leads, 2 min closing and immediate asks.
- Breakout rooms by function for owners to capture decisions.

Core sections to include in slide/note (max 5 bullets)
- Northstar metric & current delta vs plan (concrete number).
- Root cause hypothesis for any drift (data point + single probable cause).
- Immediate mitigation (72 hr ask) and owner.
- Decision required: yes/no and level (exec/team).
- Visible signal we will use to confirm recovery in 7 days.

Draft OKR touchpoints (examples - intentionally concise)
- OKR 1: Improve hosted API p95 latency by 12% by EoQ. Current: +8% over baseline. Hypothesis: batching config regression after runtime release. 72hr ask: roll back kernel selection experiment on canary nodes. Owner: infra lead.
- OKR 2: Reduce unit inference cost for standard prompt patterns by 15%. Current spend trajectory +4% vs target. Hypothesis: prefix caching not configured for several enterprise routes. 72hr ask: enable route-level prefix cache for 2 top routes. Owner: product ops.
- OKR 3: Increase private deployment uptake (closed deals) by 30% QoQ. Current pipeline gap: two stalled proofs. 72hr ask: assign 1 solutions principal to unblock each stalled POC and provide a technical checklist. Owner: solutions eng.

Risk register (quick bullets)
- Resource: Dedicated capacity overcommit due to misforecast. Short ask: temporary burst pool quota until forecasting corrected.
- Quality: Regression in response quality after quantization setting change. Short ask: re-run 20 sample evals from critical prompts.
- Compliance: Customer requiring on-prem audit artifacts earlier than planned. Short ask: prioritize audit artifact generation in private-deployments roadmap.

Decision matrix for execs to review (two quick axes)
- Impact vs Effort classification for each 72hr ask. Pick high-impact/low-effort first.
- If two asks compete for the same owner, execs decide prioritization or assign temp reinforcements.

Comms for all-staff (what they'd see Tuesday)
- TLDR header: why we ran a 72hr refocus. 2 lines max.
- Snapshot: 3 metrics and arrows (uptick/downtick).
- Clear asks and owners listed.
- Link to follow-up thread and decision tracker.

Post-all-staff follow-up plan (immediate)
- 48hr decision tracker update by owners.
- 7 day recovery check-in via async report to #northstar-72hr-refocus.
- If not recovered in 7 days, escalate to exec weekly cadence for deeper remediation.

Open questions / things to decide now
- Do we run a hard rollback for the runtime kernel change or attempt a targeted canary-only patch? Pros/cons should be documented in the canary PR.
- Can solutions eng allocate one SRE for each high-touch POC for 2 weeks? Tradeoff: pulls from SRE runway.
- Who signs the external comms for customers affected by temporary performance variance? Suggested: Head of Support + Product marketer.

Notes to self (presentation prep)
- Keep language non-technical for the all-staff top slide. Save the technical detail for the breakout notes.
- Use real numbers not percentages when possible. Ops loves concrete token counts.
- Callouts: name owners with slack handles to reduce confusion.

Appendix (data snippets to paste into slides)
- Hosted API p95 last 14 days: 420ms median, 580ms p95, baseline target 520ms.
- Dedicated capacity utilization: active pools 68%, projected peak week 92% without action.
- Private deployment POC status: 3 active, 2 stalled at security checklist.

Links and references
- Confluence northstar thread for deeper context: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Northstar-Thread
- Jira intake for asks: JIRA-OPS-4123
- Roadmap PR with rollout notes: https://github.com/redwood/roadmap/pull/78

Next steps for owners
- By EOD Monday: upload slide or note to this doc and ping execs for eyeballs.
- By Tuesday 09:30 PT: ensure presenters in place and rehearsal completed.

Quick wins list (things that can be done in 72 hours)
- Re-enable prefix cache for top 2 routes.
- Roll back kernel selection experiment on 10% of canary nodes.
- Generate audit artifact skeleton for private-deployments POC.
- Draft customer message template for support to use if variance persists.

End notes
- This is intentionally tight and slightly rough. Goal is speed and clarity. Expect many comments. I will consolidate Monday morning and mark final asks.
